title: Non-Gaussian transport in tempered fractional Laplace motion
authors: Yiming Zhao, Wei Wang, Ralf Metzler
abstract: We study a minimal stochastic model for active transport featuring a non-Gaussian displacement probability density function and transient superdiffusion. Our approach is based on a combination of an exponential tempering in the parental fractional Brownian noise correlations, augmented by a gamma-distribution of the diffusivity across the ensemble. For the resulting tempered fractional Laplace motion we derive analytical expressions for the mean-squared displacement, the kurtosis, the non-Gaussianity parameter and the displacement probability density function. We also show via stochastic simulations that the model quantitatively reproduces the main experimental observations in a recent study of active cargo particle transport by a carpet of amoeba cells.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive stochastic model for active transport, aiming to explain the complex crossover from superdiffusive to normal diffusion while maintaining non-Gaussian statistics. It achieves this by combining three distinct physical mechanisms: exponential tempering of correlations, random temporal fluctuations via a Gamma clock, and spatial disorder modeled by a Gamma diffusivity distribution. The model provides a quantitative fit to experimental data from amoeba cell transport.
main_problem: The study focuses on developing a minimal stochastic model to describe non-Gaussian transport and transient superdiffusion observed in active matter systems.
main_result: The proposed model successfully derives analytical expressions and simulations showing that the combination of exponential tempering, Lévy-Gamma subordination, and Gamma-distributed diffusivities reproduces the full experimental crossover behavior.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for key observables (MSD, kurtosis, PDF) by combining three stochastic ingredients: tempered fractional Brownian motion, a Gamma-distributed random clock, and a Gamma-distributed diffusivity.
model_or_system: The model describes active cargo particle transport by a carpet of amoeba cells, treating the dynamics as a combination of correlated motion (FBM with tempering), temporal fluctuations (Lévy-Gamma subordination), and spatial heterogeneity (Gamma diffusivity).
key_observables: Mean-Squared Displacement (MSD), Kurtosis ($\kappa(t)$), Non-Gaussianity parameter, and the displacement Probability Density Function (PDF).
important_parameters: Hurst exponent ($H$), Tempering cutoff time ($	au$), Gamma process parameters ($\eta, \lambda$), and Diffusivity parameters ($\alpha, D_ eta$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes that the three components—tempering, Lévy-Gamma subordination, and Gamma diffusivity—are all necessary to capture the full complexity observed experimentally.

paper_structure: The paper builds from the general context of anomalous diffusion in active matter, introduces the need for a multi-component model, derives the mathematical framework combining the three stochastic elements, and validates the results through analytical derivations and stochastic simulations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical active matter, the mathematical machinery involving fractional processes, subordination, and non-equilibrium statistical descriptions of transport is highly relevant to understanding dissipation and dynamics in complex quantum many-body systems or open quantum systems.
